title.narrative: Level of improvement of CT and TOC intelligence gathering techniques attributable to project activities

description.narrative: This indicator measures the improvement in CT and TOC intelligence gathering techniques, provided through training to Law Enforcement Agencies officers in charge of intelligence gathering.

comment.narrative: CT and TOC intelligence gathering techniques have been provided through training however they are in the process of being adopted by Law Enforcement Agencies officers in charge of intelligence gathering. In this regard the WAPIS information gathering template has been used as a model in the training sessions aiming to sensitize officers about its use and the expected expansion of the WAPIS database to the Northern regions throughout the project lifespan. During the next six months a WAPIS pilot will be tested in the Northern Region to assess the most appropriate ways to improve CT and TOC intelligence gathering.

comment.narrative: The Security and Intelligence Services Act was passed in October 2020. During the Inception phase the project team will check with the DSC and RSC chairmen whether they have integrated community leaders already.The already established RPCs and RHCs have limited capacities in the area of peacebuilding and mediationFour out of five RPCs established in five northernmost regions of GhanaFour out of five RHCs established in five northernmost regions of Ghana

Eventhough few DISECs have appointed some representatives it is unclear what criteria was used in selecting these appointees. A survey by the action have revealed that some DISEC chairperson have a poor appreciation of the New Intelligence Act which requires them to do the appointments. Also security agencies do not also trust civilians ability to manage sensitive security information. Others reported that the lack of resources to cater for additional appointees is a contributing factor for the exclusion of community leaders. An average of three initiatives each from the 15 CSOs have been carried out within the period. 121 more chiefs and queen mothers have benefitted from ADR Chieftaincy Act and Succession and Land Management training provided by the Action. A total of 462 chiefs and queen mothers have benefitted in all trainings.

title.narrative: Decrease of the number of violent incidents per region

description.narrative: Decrease of the number of violent incidents per region

comment.narrative: During the project some violent incidents have rejuvenated in recorded areas. These include Reprisal attacks between conflicting parties in Bawku i.e. the Kusasis and Mamprusis a different dimension has been attacks on public transport vehicles buses in the Walewale enclave Agropastoral conflicts involving fulbe and farmers in host communities e.g. Tumu BongoSoe Nabdam Bolgatanga Bawku Pusiga Land disputes between the Mamprusis and Gonjas in Lukula in the Savannah region Youth riots in Senior High Schools SHS Sandema SHS Bolgatanga Technical Institute Bawku Technical Institute Fumbisi Agricultural Senior High School Sirigu Integrated Senior High School Notwithstanding the above pockets of conflicts and incidence of violence all regionsareas with previous incidence have remained relatively calm. The NPC has not updated the conflict map to prove otherwise. This could be attributed to curfews imposed by government and complemented by the nonkinetic peacebuilding approaches supported by the action through the NationalRegional Peace Councils Regional House of Chiefs and CSOs.
